CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFSEARCH

CFSEARCH runs a search against collections filled by CFINDEX and returns the matching documents, best first, as a query object you can display with CFOUTPUT.

Category

Verity search

Syntax

<CFSEARCH NAME="search_name"
    COLLECTION="collection_name"
    TYPE="SIMPLE"
    CRITERIA="search_expression"
    MAXROWS="number"
    STARTROW="row_number"
    EXTERNAL="Yes/No"
    LANGUAGE="English">

Attributes

NAME
Required. Name of the query that receives the results.
COLLECTION
Required. One collection, or several separated by commas.
TYPE
Optional, default "SIMPLE". SIMPLE or EXPLICIT. KoldFusion understands the simple syntax; in explicit criteria, operators in angle brackets such as <NEAR> are skipped and the remaining words are searched with the simple rules.
CRITERIA
Optional. The search expression (see Usage). Empty criteria return no rows.
MAXROWS
Optional, default all. Maximum number of rows to return.
STARTROW
Optional, default "1". First match to return; use it with MAXROWS to show results a page at a time.
EXTERNAL
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
LANGUAGE
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.

Usage

The result query has the columns URL, Key, Title, Score, Custom1, Custom2, Summary and RecordsSearched, plus the usual RecordCount, CurrentRow and ColumnList. Score runs from 0 to 0.98 relative to the best match; Summary holds the first 250 characters of the document text.

Criteria Finds documents containing
web database both words (AND is implied; you may also write it)
web, database either word (OR works too)
"safety goggles" the exact phrase
chemistry NOT organic chemistry but not organic
crypt* words matching the wildcard; ? matches one character

Matching ignores case, and a trailing "s" still matches (course finds "courses"). Words in a title count three times as much as words in the body.

Note  Inside CFOUTPUT, write #Results.URL# rather than #URL#: on its own, URL means the URL scope.

If a collection does not exist, CFSEARCH throws an error. Pass user input straight to CRITERIA; it is not SQL, so there is nothing to escape.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFPARAM NAME="Form.Criteria" DEFAULT="web">

<!--- Set up the course index (see CFINDEX) so this page stands alone --->
<CFTRY>
  <CFCOLLECTION ACTION="CREATE" COLLECTION="snippets">
<CFCATCH TYPE="Any"></CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
<CFQUERY NAME="GetCourses" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT Course_ID, Dept_ID, CorName, CorLevel, CorDesc FROM CourseList
</CFQUERY>
<CFINDEX COLLECTION="snippets" ACTION="UPDATE" QUERY="GetCourses"
    KEY="Course_ID" TITLE="CorName" BODY="CorName,CorDesc"
    CUSTOM1="Dept_ID" CUSTOM2="CorLevel">

<CFSEARCH NAME="Results" COLLECTION="snippets"
    CRITERIA="#Form.Criteria#" MAXROWS="10">

<CFOUTPUT>
<FORM ACTION="cfsearch.cfm" METHOD="POST">
Search the course catalog:
<INPUT TYPE="Text" NAME="Criteria" VALUE="#HTMLEditFormat(Form.Criteria)#" SIZE="25">
<INPUT TYPE="Submit" VALUE="Search"><BR>
<FONT SIZE="1">Try: chemistry NOT organic, "safety goggles", crypt*, web, database</FONT>
</FORM>
<P>#Results.RecordCount# match(es) for <B>#HTMLEditFormat(Form.Criteria)#</B>
</CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Score</TH><TH>Course</TH><TH>Dept</TH><TH>Level</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Results">
<TR><TD>#Score#</TD><TD>#Title#</TD><TD>#Custom1#</TD><TD>#Custom2#</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
